title: The condominium-conversion lottery, as the code writes it
question: How does the condominium-conversion lottery decide who wins, and when could it run again?
finding: At most 200 units a year are chosen by lottery (Subdivision Code 1396). The seniority procedure in 1396.3, which prevails over the original 1396.1, gives each losing building an extra ticket for every lottery it lost, with no cap (1396.1 had capped tickets at five), and puts buildings that lost three or more times into a Pool A of up to 100 units ranked by how often they lost. So a rising chance of winning for repeat entrants is what the rule is designed to produce. No lottery could be held before 1 January 2024 (1396.5).
how: Sections 1396 to 1396.5 of the Subdivision Code, read from the full-text export; quotations checked word for word.
limits: Tickets are earned by losing, not by years of owner occupancy; occupancy decides eligibility (three years for two- to four-unit buildings). The lotteries screen’s summary of the rule ("ticket pools by years of owner occupancy") should be read with that correction. Whether the lottery has resumed depends on reports that are not on disk.

rows.rule: At most 200 units a year may be approved for conversion, chosen by Public Works lottery from eligible two- to six-unit buildings whose owners have lived there the required years.
rows.quote: a maximum of 200 units as selected yearly by lottery by the Department of Public Works from all eligible applicants

rows.rule: Under the original procedure, a Pool B building gets one ticket for the current lottery plus one for each earlier lottery it lost (at most one for 1990-94), and no more than five tickets.
rows.quote: No building in Pool B shall receive more than five tickets.

rows.rule: The seniority procedure prevails over 1396.1: Pool A takes buildings that lost three or more lotteries, ranked in classes by how many times they lost, up to 100 units; in Pool B each building gets one ticket plus one for every lottery it lost, with no five-ticket cap.
rows.quote: shall prevail over the lottery selection process of Section 1396.1 for the conversion of residential units

rows.rule: Pool B ticket rule under the seniority procedure.
rows.quote: plus one lottery ticket for every lottery in which the building participated but failed to be selected for conversion
rows.verdict: Confirmed: chances rise with each loss, by rule

rows.rule: No conversion application may be accepted and no lottery held before 1 January 2024; the lottery then resumes the first February after the housing office reports enough replacement units, or at the end of a maximum suspension period set by the number of expedited conversions.
rows.quote: nor conduct a lottery under this Article prior to January 1, 2024
rows.verdict: Partly: the code sets the conditions; whether they were met needs the Public Works and housing-office reports
